newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: YTL Power up after China project nod.
newsitem.headline: YTL Power up after China project nod.

text.p: Shares of YTL Power International Bhd gained on heavy volume on Tuesday following news that its power project in China has been approved, but several analysts said they are not changing their ratings.
The company said on Monday that its Nanchang, China project has been approved by Chinese authorities.

YTL Power has a 51 percent stake in YTL-CPI, the joint venture company with China Power Investment Holding Co Ltd (CPI). YTL Power and CPI have signed a joint venture pact to develop and own generation facilities in Nanchang, Jiangxi province.

YTL Power's stock is up "on the approval (of the China project) and the listing," said an institutional dealer at a local brokerage, referring to YTL Power's comment on Monday that it may list shares of its Chinese and African units.
At 0405 GMT, YTL Power was up eight cents to 3.74 ringgit, on volume of over 4.7 million shares. It traded as high as 3.82 ringgit and was among the top most active stocks.
"We maintain that YTLPI is fairly valued at 4.00 ringgit even with the approval of the Nanchang power project," said a report by Jupiter Securities issued on Tuesday.

With the acquisition of two existing 125 MW power plants in Nanchang, YTL Power should see an added 26.1 million ringgit in profits a year, Jupiter estimated. With an extended 550 MW of power from a new plant, the profit contribution should be 61.2 million ringgit a year, it said.
For the year ended June 30, 1996, YTL Power posted net profit of 371.4 million ringgit or 19.5 cents a share.
Thong & Kay Hian, in a report issued on Tuesday, said it was keeping a long-term buy recommendation on YTL Power.
"Upside in the share price hinges on YTLPI's new projects and to a large extent, on management's ability to deliver," said Thong & Kay Hian.

The African project involves the proposed privatisation of the Hwange Power Station in Zimbabwe through a joint venture firm that is 51 percent owned by YTL Power. YTL Power is still waiting for Zimbabwean government approval for the project.
